test_cases.test_name: X-bar/R Chart Creation and Basic Functionality Test
test_cases.objective: To verify that the SPC dashboard can successfully create X-bar/R control charts from a CSV input file and apply the vendor's standard Nelson rules for out-of-control detection.
prerequisites: SPC dashboard software is installed and accessible
Test CSV file with valid QC data (subgroups and measurements) is available
User account with 'Analyst' role permissions is created and active

test_steps.action: Log into the SPC dashboard using the pre-configured 'Analyst' user credentials.
test_steps.expected_result: User successfully authenticates and the main dashboard interface loads without errors.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the login screen and main dashboard

test_steps.action: Navigate to the 'New Chart' menu and select the option to create an X-bar/R chart.
test_steps.expected_result: The system displays a dialog or wizard for configuring a new X-bar/R chart.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the chart creation interface

test_steps.action: Select the pre-prepared test CSV file as the data source and map the required columns (subgroup ID, measurements).
test_steps.expected_result: The system accepts the CSV file and correctly maps the data columns for chart generation.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the data mapping configuration

test_steps.action: Enable the 'Apply Nelson Rules' option in the chart configuration and confirm the settings.
test_steps.expected_result: The system generates the X-bar and R charts, displaying control limits and points flagged by Nelson rules.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the final rendered charts with Nelson rule violations highlighted

test_steps.action: Use the built-in annotation tool to add a comment to a specific data point on the chart.
test_steps.expected_result: The comment is successfully saved and is visible when hovering over or selecting the annotated point.
data_to_capture: Screenshot showing the added comment on the chart

acceptance_criteria: X-bar and R charts are rendered correctly with accurate control limits calculated from the input data.
Nelson rules are applied and visually indicate out-of-control points as specified by the vendor.
Data point annotation feature functions as expected, allowing users to add and view comments.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 211.68 requires automated equipment to reliably perform intended functions.
General principles of data integrity (ALCOA+) for the generated chart configurations and annotations.
data_integrity_requirements: The chart configuration (control limits, rules applied) must be retained as a controlled record.
Any annotations added to the chart must be permanently associated with the data point.
urs_requirements: URS-020-001: Users shall create X-bar/R and p-charts from CSV inputs.
URS-020-002: Users shall apply vendor's standard Nelson rules.
URS-020-005: Users shall annotate points with comments using built-in features.
URS-020-008: Retain chart configurations as controlled records.

test_cases.test_name: Role-Based Access Control and Data Export Verification
test_cases.objective: To validate that the system correctly enforces role-based view access for released datasets and allows authorized export of data to PDF and CSV formats.
prerequisites: SPC dashboard is installed and running
A dataset has been marked as 'Released' within the system
Two user accounts are created: one with 'Viewer' role and one with 'Analyst' role

test_steps.action: Log into the SPC dashboard using the 'Viewer' role user credentials.
test_steps.expected_result: User successfully logs in and is presented with a read-only interface.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the dashboard view for the 'Viewer' role

test_steps.action: Attempt to access the pre-released dataset and try to edit any data points or chart configurations.
test_steps.expected_result: The system prevents any modifications and displays a message indicating read-only access.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the error or notification message when edit is attempted

test_steps.action: Navigate to the released chart and use the vendor's standard export function to generate a PDF report.
test_steps.expected_result: A PDF file is generated containing the chart image and relevant statistics, saved to the specified location.
data_to_capture: The generated PDF file for review

test_steps.action: Use the export function to export the underlying chart data to a CSV file.
test_steps.expected_result: A CSV file containing the data points, control limits, and any flags is successfully created.
data_to_capture: The generated CSV file for review

test_steps.action: Log out and then log in using the 'Analyst' role user credentials. Attempt to modify the released dataset.
test_steps.expected_result: The system prevents the 'Analyst' from modifying the released data, enforcing read-only access for all roles.
data_to_capture: Screenshot confirming edit attempts are blocked for the Analyst role on released data

acceptance_criteria: The 'Viewer' role has read-only access to all data and cannot make changes.
Released datasets are immutable and cannot be edited by any user role.
Export functions (PDF and CSV) operate correctly and generate complete, accurate files.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11.10(d) requires limiting system access to authorized individuals.
URS-020-007 specifies read-only access for released datasets to ensure data integrity.
data_integrity_requirements: Exported data (PDF/CSV) must be a complete and accurate representation of the on-screen data.
Access controls must be robust to prevent unauthorized modification of released data.
urs_requirements: URS-020-003: The system shall provide vendor standard export to PDF and CSV.
URS-020-004: The dashboard shall allow role-based view access.
URS-020-007: Read-only access for released datasets.

test_cases.objective: To verify that the dashboard correctly restricts data views based on user roles as defined in the system configuration.
prerequisites: Dashboard software is installed and configured
At least two distinct user roles are configured (e.g., Viewer, Analyst)
Test datasets are loaded and available
User accounts for each role type are created

test_steps.action: Log into the dashboard using an account with 'Viewer' role permissions.
test_steps.expected_result: Login is successful and the dashboard home screen is displayed.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the dashboard home screen

test_steps.action: Attempt to access the chart creation module and modify an existing chart configuration.
test_steps.expected_result: The system prevents access to modification functions or displays a permissions error message.
data_to_capture: Record of actions attempted and system response

test_steps.action: Log out and then log in using an account with 'Analyst' or higher privileges.
test_steps.expected_result: Login is successful and the dashboard home screen is displayed with additional menu options.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the dashboard home screen
List of visible menu options compared to Viewer role

test_steps.action: Navigate to the chart creation module and confirm the ability to modify configurations.
test_steps.expected_result: The system allows full access to chart creation and modification functions without errors.

acceptance_criteria: Users with 'Viewer' role cannot access chart modification functions.
Users with 'Analyst' role (or higher) can successfully access and modify chart configurations.
The system consistently enforces role-based permissions across all relevant modules.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 - Controls for limited access to systems and data
Annex 11 - Privileges for amending data should be restricted to authorized persons
data_integrity_requirements: Access controls must prevent unauthorized modification of chart configurations and data.
User role assignments must be accurately enforced by the system.

test_cases.objective: To verify that the vendor's built-in scheduler correctly generates and emails reports according to a predefined schedule.
prerequisites: Dashboard software is installed and configured with email server settings
A valid email account is configured for receiving test reports
A report template (e.g., X-bar chart) is created and saved
The scheduler feature is accessible to the test user

test_steps.action: Navigate to the scheduler configuration module within the dashboard.
test_steps.expected_result: The scheduler interface loads successfully, showing options to create a new scheduled task.

test_steps.action: Configure a new scheduled report task to run in 5 minutes, selecting a pre-configured report and specifying the test email address as the recipient.
test_steps.expected_result: The system accepts the configuration and confirms the scheduled task has been created.
data_to_capture: Details of the scheduled task configuration

test_steps.action: Wait for the scheduled time to elapse and then check the specified email inbox for the report.
test_steps.expected_result: The email is received within a reasonable time after the scheduled run time, containing the correct report in the specified format (PDF or CSV).
data_to_capture: Verification of report attachment and content

test_steps.action: Verify the content and format of the attached report matches the original configuration.
test_steps.expected_result: The attached report is complete, accurate, and matches the format and data of the original configured report.

acceptance_criteria: The scheduler successfully creates a scheduled task without errors.
The system generates and emails the report at the scheduled time.
The emailed report is complete, accurate, and in the correct format.
The entire process functions using the vendor's standard, unmodified scheduler.
regulatory_basis: General GAMP principle for verifying automated processes
Annex 11 - Accuracy and reliability of automated data processing
data_integrity_requirements: The scheduled report must accurately reflect the current data and configuration at the time of generation.
The email delivery process must not alter the content or format of the report.

test_cases.test_name: Performance Testing for Large Dataset Loading and Chart Rendering
test_cases.objective: Verify the system meets performance requirements for loading large datasets and rendering charts within specified time limits under supported hardware conditions.
prerequisites: OQ-001 Installation Verification completed successfully
Test environment with vendor-supported hardware specifications
Prepared CSV file containing exactly 100,000 data points
User account with appropriate permissions to create charts

test_steps.action: Log into the SPC dashboard with valid credentials and navigate to the data import section.
test_steps.expected_result: User successfully logs in and accesses the data import functionality.

test_steps.action: Upload the CSV file containing 100,000 data points and initiate the import process while starting a timer.
test_steps.expected_result: System begins processing the file and displays a progress indicator.

test_steps.action: Stop the timer when the dataset is fully loaded and available for chart creation.
test_steps.expected_result: Dataset loads completely and is ready for analysis within 5 seconds.

test_steps.action: Apply filters to the loaded dataset and initiate chart rendering while starting a timer.
test_steps.expected_result: System begins processing the filter changes and rendering the updated chart.

test_steps.action: Stop the timer when the chart is fully rendered and interactive.
test_steps.expected_result: Chart renders completely and becomes interactive within 2 seconds after filter changes.

acceptance_criteria: Dataset containing 100,000 points loads in less than 5 seconds
Charts render completely in less than 2 seconds after filter changes
No performance degradation or system crashes during testing
All functionality remains responsive during and after performance testing
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for system performance and reliability
GAMP 5 guidelines for performance qualification of standard software
data_integrity_requirements: All 100,000 data points must be accurately loaded without corruption
Chart calculations must reflect the complete dataset accurately
Filtered views must maintain data integrity and mathematical accuracy
urs_requirements: URS-020-010: Load 100k data points in < 5 seconds on supported hardware
URS-020-011: Render charts in < 2 seconds after filter changes
